title: The first known film shot from an aeroplane was made in 1909, with Wilbur Wright flying

cover.alt: Grainy black-and-white frame filmed from a 1909 Wright Flyer: a strut and a bar of the aircraft cross the view of dark ground just after take-off.
cover.credit: Société Générale des Cinématographes Eclipse · Public domain

body: On 24 April 1909, at what is now Centocelle Airport near Rome, the French film company Eclipse filmed Wilbur Wright demonstrating his Flyer. For part of the film the camera rode on the aircraft itself, mounted on the lower left wing near Wright’s seat. The result, known in Germany as *Wilbur Wright und seine Flugmaschine*, is considered the first motion-picture aerial photography from a **heavier-than-air** aircraft: a plane, not a balloon. Not long before, some European papers had dismissed the Wrights’ claims of flight as a ‘bluff’.

slides.alt: Grainy black-and-white film shot from a 1909 Wright Flyer: the ground drops away after take-off, then the horizon tilts and fields slide past below, framed by the aircraft’s struts and wires.
slides.caption: Near Rome, 24 April 1909: a camera on Wilbur Wright’s Flyer records the lift-off, then the horizon and fields sliding past, framed by the plane’s struts.
